title: Memories that fade and sensors that remember
seoTitle: Memories that fade and sensors that remember | Blog, Jorge Parra
description: A photonic chip with fading memory, a simulated phase-change device and a sensor that briefly retains traces of movement.

title: Light learns to travel, remember and change direction
description: What can a material do with the light it receives? Depending on the material, it can modulate light on a chip, retain a trace of its passage or separate two polarisations in the infrared.

title: Light on a chip, ions in a pore and spins in a crystal
description: A symmetric pore lets more ions through in one direction than the other. Alongside the reason why, this week’s experiments reveal where a germanosilicate guide loses light and how long a spin keeps its phase in a perovskite.

title: On-demand photons and two ways to test materials with heat
description: Heating a memory during fabrication can improve its response, whereas cycling a perovskite solar cell through hot and cold degrades it. For this week’s quantum source, the test of repeatability is whether two photons emitted in succession interfere.

title: Measuring a spectrum, orienting a monolayer and making gold porous
description: Changing the shape of a film can alter what happens when light falls on it. Compare compact and porous gold, watch a MoS₂ monolayer acquire its orientation as it grows, and see how thin flakes let a detector reconstruct a spectrum.

title: Lasers, vision and fluctuating memories
description: A reflection can disturb a laser, while the noise in a memory cell can tell us about the material that stores the bit. Between those two papers, a photosynapse makes use of another easily overlooked detail, the orientation of the light it receives.

title: A two-cycle pulse, a light-sensitive synapse and multilevel memory
description: An infrared pulse is so brief that its field oscillates only twice. A photosynapse distinguishes the orientation of light and a ferroelectric crystal retains several resistance levels, two ways for information to outlast the stimulus.

title: Sensing heat with light and adjusting current with charge or a field
description: Acetylene gives itself away by releasing heat beside an optical waveguide. Two other signals can be tuned before they are read, by sharing charge between memory gates or by rotating a field relative to a magnetic interface.

title: A gradual image, a delayed neuron and two twisted crystals
description: An image that appears gradually and an electrode that delays a neuron’s response use time in different ways. Join two lithium niobate crystals and the setting to adjust is the angle, which can change how dipoles arrange themselves at the boundary.

title: Light between two metals, power on a thin film and a blue diode
description: A volt across a near-atomic gap can make a big difference to the light coming out. At different scales, thin-film transistors deliver power to large arrays, and a molecule on a nanocrystal surface helps keep an LED blue.

title: Networks for light and protons, and an insulator with grain boundaries
description: In an optical network, paths are designed for light. A nickelate network uses moving protons to remember, while the third paper looks for a path best avoided, the one a leakage current might take between grains.

title: Mixing light and magnetism, storing charge and watching an LED age
description: An LED deteriorating under the microscope reveals which interface fails first. Meanwhile, a lattice of resonators concentrates the interaction between microwaves and magnetism, and a capacitor brings memory closer to the site of an optical calculation.

title: Circular light, memory in a synapse and amorphous regions written in a crystal
description: Circularly polarised light is a way to probe how excitons respond in a metasurface. The other papers follow what remains after the signal, from a state retained by a synapse to a region of a crystal that has lost its order.

title: An infrared modulator, a fault-tolerant memory and a ferroelectric solar cell
description: A lithium niobate modulator carries the signal into the mid-infrared. Factoring in circuit faults helps a memory retrieve more patterns, while in a solar cell the site where charges are separated helps determine how much is lost along the way.

title: Polarisation in a film, avalanche in a transistor and a transition in VO₂
description: A pulse changes how a film responds to polarised light, while a transistor channel directs the flow of charge. With VO₂, the question is how quickly the material changes and how to follow the transition from within.

title: Computing with light, switching functions with voltage and bending a compound eye
description: Putting 185 pixels on a curved surface means deciding where the film can bend. Two other design choices round out the edition, connecting an optical processor to a neural network and making a device change its job with a voltage.

title: Continuous terahertz waves, an ionic photosynapse and domain walls
description: Two infrared lasers produce a signal that can be tuned in the terahertz range. In a photosynapse it is ions that move, while in an oxide the surprise lies at the boundary where two kinds of electrical order meet.

title: Photonics for listening to the spectrum, current for switching a magnet and gold between layers
description: A chip tells which radio frequencies are occupied in less than 110 nanoseconds. The other papers look at what happens when layers meet, whether to switch a magnet with current or fit gold atoms inside an oxide.

title: Reflecting polaritons, a graphene gate and dipoles that turn
description: How far does a wave travel before reflecting off the edge of a flake? Thin layers let us ask that question and two others, how a graphene gate controls a molecular monolayer and how the polarisation of a material can be turned.

title: Shrinking a pattern, separating noise and bringing an exciton into view
description: How do you carve a void smaller than the tool that draws it? One answer is to shrink the entire piece afterwards. The other studies follow an audio signal buried in noise and a dark exciton whose emission becomes visible when a ferroelectric layer is added.

title: A wireless link, a magnetic junction and photons from an edge
description: A wireless link retains part of its carrier to give the receiver a reference. At much smaller scales a magnetic junction accumulates pulses, while the edge of a perovskite provides a site for single-photon emission.

title: Trimming a finished chip, storing states in a molecule and watching quantum dots
description: A carbon deposit adjusts the path of light in a chip after fabrication. Control extends down to a single molecule in the memory study, while understanding why an array of quantum dots blinks calls for watching several emitters together.

title: Growing quantum dots to order, building a neuron and choosing a crystal’s faces
description: Centring a quantum dot in its resonator starts before the resonator is built. How a perovskite grows also changes its blue emission, and between those two papers a set of nanowires shows how an artificial neuron takes shape.

title: Pulses in silicon nitride, stretchable memory and emitters acting together
description: A silicon nitride circuit produces intense light pulses. The other papers use light to write into a stretchable transistor and to see what happens when emitters in a perovskite respond together.

title: A liquid-crystal shutter and two ways to use a magnet
description: A liquid crystal adjusts the brightness of quantum dots while their colour stays the same. Two other papers make use of a magnet, letting it fluctuate to explore a computation or tuning the coupling between its layers to control spin waves.

title: Optical cells, deflected currents and light taking a different path
description: A light signal can change a cell’s role between neuron and synapse. The other two papers follow signals that are deflected, an electric current at a magnetic interface and a beam steered with little loss.

title: A flat fibre and two devices for working with images
description: What if some image processing happens before the image is sent? A transistor retains the light response and a film selects the full scene or just its edges. Elsewhere, flattening a fibre opens up another way to fit it into a setup.

title: A dispersive lens, a light-sensitive fingerprint and a magnetoelectric oxide
description: A distance sensor puts chromatic aberration to work by bringing each colour to a different focus. Colour also changes the electronic fingerprint of a MoS₂ circuit, while a magnetic field provides a handle on the polarization of a hafnia film.

title: Polarization, memory and perovskites
description: An optical circuit works both ways, preparing polarisation and measuring it when the path is reversed. The other papers simplify things at different stages, putting a learning rule into a memristor and reducing defects as a perovskite grows.

title: A waveguide that processes light, flexible transistors and a field-responsive glass
description: The same MoS₂ sheet can guide light and change the signal it carries. A flexible semiconductor can also support two kinds of transistor, while a molecular glass responds differently to light and an electric field.

title: Side entry into a waveguide, activity in a neuron and an emitting monolayer
description: Openings in the wall of a hollow guide give access to the region the light travels through. Also in this edition are a VO₂ neuron that adjusts its activity and an organic laser that keeps emitting under continuous illumination.

title: Radio beams, microwave computing and plasmons in a crystal
description: A wave’s path can be part of the design. A photonic network steers radio beams, a microwave circuit uses the signal’s journey to compute, and in a crystal the material itself favours plasmons travelling in one direction.

title: Reflections for reading a spectrum, motion memory and two responses from one element
description: A waveguide full of small reflections holds clues to the light that entered it. In the other papers, a zinc oxide memory picks up information about motion, and one element distinguishes optical signals that would be hard to separate by intensity alone.

title: Writing an infrared image, storing charge and thinning silver
description: An infrared image can be written pixel by pixel, while a memory retains a state through charge-density waves. Scale matters again in the third paper, which measures how silver’s response to light changes as the film gets thinner.

title: A shortcut for light, event-based vision and colour from infrared
description: A shortcut changes where light travels on a chip. The other two studies change what we can do with it, from detecting changes in a scene to getting several infrared photons to produce visible light.

title: Polaritons along edges, languages in an array and light-activated memory
description: Polarisation can select which edge a polariton follows, while in indium selenide light helps write a memory state. The third paper turns to text and how to split language recognition between an algorithm and a memristor array.

title: A nonlinear metasurface, high-temperature vision and an adjustable Hall response
description: Detecting visible light at 450 °C is one of this week’s tests. The other two explore how far a signal can be controlled, transforming light with a metasurface and changing a material’s Hall response from a neighbouring ferroelectric layer.

title: Carrying high-frequency signals, filtering spikes and forming vortices
description: Sending signals above a hundred gigahertz and preparing input for a spiking network raise different questions about what survives along the way. In the third paper, the feature of interest is inside a ferroelectric, where dipoles form vortices on silicon.

title: Computing with light, retaining polarisation and turning a mask into an emitter
description: A modulator retains its setting when the voltage is removed, and a ferroelectric film preserves loops of polarization as it moves from one substrate to another. To pattern luminous pixels, the third team makes the photosensitive layer itself emit light.

title: Cavities on a fiber, graphene electrodes and ion channels
description: A small change in geometry can determine where a signal goes. A slight variation in fibre radius traps light, two graphene edges define where a memory switches, and a channel lets ions through while keeping excess water out.

title: A spin read by light, a magnet that remembers it and a stable dielectric
description: Light can read a hole spin or write states into a magnet. In both cases the question is how long the effect lasts, and the third paper explores a different kind of stability by testing how a dielectric responds as the temperature changes.

title: Light beneath a monolayer, carbon dots and heat in a ferroelectric
description: Below a monolayer, light can be concentrated. On top of a semiconductor, carbon dots prepare the surface for an insulator. The third paper follows a less visible but equally necessary path, the one heat takes to escape from a ferroelectric film.

title: Infrared in a suspended guide, a reconfigurable transistor and the first steps of crystal growth
description: Removing the substrate brings modulation into an infrared range where some of the light would otherwise be lost in it. The other papers adjust devices at different points, choosing what a finished transistor does or intervening just as a crystal starts to grow.

title: A silicon modulator and two ways to use perovskites
description: A silicon modulator corrects part of the signal before sending it. Two other papers take a close look at perovskites, asking why the same device can store information in two ways and how the pace of crystallisation affects an LED film.

title: Separating light modes, stabilizing transistors and tracking electrons in graphene
description: Two light fields can have equal intensity and different spatial coherence, a distinction an optical circuit can resolve. One team follows electrons in graphene through an optical cycle, while another uses an additive to alter the path charges take through a perovskite.

title: Moiré light, memory on two timescales and emission from a defect
description: Two almost aligned light patterns draw a moiré in mid-air, and an atomic defect leaves its own signature in a monolayer’s light. Between those experiments, a transistor shows what remains of a signal after a moment and what lasts longer.

title: Light and sound on a chip, stacked transistors and an infrared image
description: How much can a device change when you remove what sits beneath it, add an insulating layer or vary a film’s thickness? This week, those choices help confine sound in an optical waveguide, stack transistors with low leakage and reveal an infrared pattern.
